member.summary: A minimal, dependency-free implementation of AWS Signature Version 4 (header-based signing), used to authenticate Bedrock requests. member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Clients.AnthropicClient
member.summary:
Anthropic (Claude) client for the Messages API.
Supported: Chat, ToolChat, and Generate (/v1/messages, generation sent as one user turn, streaming as typed SSE events), and Models (/v1/models, following pagination).
Not supported (throw ): Embed, SparseEmbed, Rerank, Classify, Decide. For embeddings with Claude, pair it with .
Auth: required API key, sent as x-api-key, plus anthropic-version and an optional anthropic-workspace-id.
Defaults: completion claude-sonnet-5-5. max_tokens is always sent (the API requires it).
Tool results are sent as user-role tool_result blocks, and consecutive results merge into one user turn. Citations on documents or search results cannot be combined with structured output (output_config.format); the API returns 400.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Clients.CliAgentClientBase
member.summary: Base class for agent harness clients: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor CLI, Mux, Pi, and OpenCode. A harness is not a model API; it is a local CLI that runs its own tool loop against the filesystem and reports agent events. This base runs the CLI as a child process (never through a shell), delivers the prompt over standard input where the CLI allows it, maps output lines to s through the client's parser, enforces the timeout and output limit by killing the whole process tree, records each process in as a , and reports telemetry. Authentication is delegated to the CLI's own login; there is no API key parameter.

This lets callers configure the transport (for example a custom that relaxes TLS certificate validation, or a proxy), and lets several clients share one connection pool. Clients never modify ; credentials and provider headers are attached to each request, so a shared client is safe to use across providers.

AWS Bedrock client. Requests are signed with AWS Signature Version 4.
Supported: Chat, ToolChat, and Generate (the Converse API, converse and converse-stream), Embed (InvokeModel with Titan or Cohere embedding models), Rerank (InvokeModel with Cohere or Amazon rerank models), and Models (control-plane /foundation-models).

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Clients.ClaudeCodeClient
member.summary:
Agent harness client for Anthropic's Claude Code CLI (claude). Each run is claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages with the prompt on standard input; a session is resumed with --resume <session_id>. The system prompt (and any system messages in the history) is passed with --append-system-prompt, so Claude Code keeps its own system prompt. Authentication is the CLI's own (claude auth login, or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment); connectivity checks it with claude auth status --json. Claude Code has no model-listing command, so this client has no ListModelsAsync.
Permission mapping (verified against Claude Code 2.1.312): uses --permission-mode dontAsk --tools Read,Glob,Grep --strict-mcp-config: only the built-in file-reading tools exist, no MCP server is loaded, and anything that would prompt is denied. uses --permission-mode dontAsk --disallowedTools Edit,Write,NotebookEdit: reads and the read-only shell commands Claude Code approves without asking run, the editing tools are denied, and anything else that would prompt is denied (allow rules in the user's own Claude Code settings still apply). uses --permission-mode acceptEdits: file edits inside the working directory run without asking and, since nobody can answer a prompt in print mode, everything else that would prompt is denied. uses --permission-mode bypassPermissions; no other mode passes it or --dangerously-skip-permissions.

member.name: M:PolyPrompt.Clients.ClaudeCodeClient.ParseLine(System.String,PolyPrompt.Clients.CliRunState)
member.summary:
Map one claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages line. Only top-level messages (parent_tool_use_id null) produce text, reasoning, and tool events; subagent traffic is ignored.
system/init {session_id, model} -> Started (session id; model is the reported model) system/compact_boundary -> Notice system/api_retry -> Notice (IsError) system/hook_*, status, thinking_tokens, other -> (none) stream_event message_start -> (none; remembers the message id) stream_event content_block_delta text_delta -> TextDelta stream_event content_block_delta thinking_delta -> ReasoningDelta stream_event other (tool input, signature, ...) -> (none) assistant {error, content[text]} -> Notice (IsError); the error code is kept for the result assistant content[text|thinking] -> TextDelta / ReasoningDelta only when no partial delta of that kind arrived for the message (partial deltas are the source) assistant content[tool_use] -> ToolUse (name, id, JSON input) user content[tool_result] -> ToolResult (ToolUse first if unseen; is_error) rate_limit_event status allowed -> (none) rate_limit_event other status -> Notice (IsError when rejected) result is_error false -> final text = result; usage, cost; Completed at exit result is_error true -> failure (error_max_turns is TurnLimitReached); usage, cost result permission_denials[] -> Notice (IsError) per denied tool call
Text: partial text_delta events build the streamed text and the assistant message repeats it, so the assistant copy is used only when no delta arrived for that message (for example a synthetic message); the final text is result.result. Usage (from result.usage): input_tokens -> PromptTokens, cache_read_input_tokens -> CachedPromptTokens, cache_creation_input_tokens -> CacheCreationTokens, output_tokens -> CompletionTokens, output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens -> ReasoningTokens. Claude Code reports no total, so TotalTokens stays null. total_cost_usd -> CostUsd exactly as reported.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Clients.CursorClient
member.summary:
Agent harness client for the Cursor CLI (cursor-agent). Each run is cursor-agent -p --output-format stream-json --stream-partial-output with the prompt on standard input (print mode reads standard input to end of file when no prompt argument is given); a session is resumed with --resume <chatId>. The installer links the same binary as both agent and cursor-agent; cursor-agent is the default here and callers can set to agent. Authentication is the CLI's own (cursor-agent login, or CURSOR_API_KEY in the environment).
Permission mapping: and use --mode ask (Cursor's read-only Q&A mode; it has no separate read-only-commands level) with --sandbox enabled. uses the default agent mode with --sandbox enabled: Cursor has no flag that allows workspace writes short of --force, so writes and commands run only where the user's or project's permission allow list (cli-config.json, .cursor/cli.json) permits them and anything that would need an approval is denied. Only passes --force (Cursor's "Run Everything"; --yolo is an alias), together with --sandbox disabled. --sandbox is a per-run override; the CLI exits with an error where its sandbox is unavailable, and a caller can append --sandbox disabled through (the last value wins). Note that Cursor also auto-approves in print mode when the user has saved "Run Everything" as their approval mode; PolyPrompt does not change the CLI's configuration, so the read-only modes rely on --mode ask in that case.
Workspace trust: print mode refuses to run in a directory the user has not trusted unless --trust or --force is passed. --trust records a saved trust decision, so this client never passes it; trust the directory once interactively, or add --trust through .
Contract sources: https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/parameters, https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/output-format, https://cursor.com/docs/cli/headless, https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/permissions, https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/authentication, https://cursor.com/docs/cli/changelog, and the command-line parser, print-mode writer, status and models commands of the published CLI package 2026.10.22-27dcf5f.

member.name: M:PolyPrompt.Clients.CursorClient.ParseLine(System.String,PolyPrompt.Clients.CliRunState)
member.summary:
Map one stream-json line.
system init {session_id, model} -> Started (session id; model is the display name) system task_notification {title, status} -> Notice system background_shell_timeout -> Notice (IsError) user -> (none; echo of the prompt) assistant with timestamp_ms, without model_call_id -> TextDelta (a streamed delta) assistant with model_call_id, or without timestamp -> (none; duplicate flush of text already streamed) thinking delta {text} -> ReasoningDelta thinking completed -> (none) tool_call started {call_id, tool_call} -> ToolUse (name is the tool_call key, or function.name) tool_call completed {call_id, tool_call.result} -> ToolResult (IsError unless the result is "success") retry starting {attempt} -> Notice (IsError) connection reconnecting {attempt} -> Notice (IsError) result success {result, session_id, usage} -> final text, usage; Completed is emitted by the base at exit result with is_error true -> failure; Failed is emitted by the base at exit interaction_query, retry resuming, connection reconnected, unknown types -> (none)
Cursor reports run errors only on standard error, after the session started; see . Usage (result.usage, the whole turn): inputTokens -> PromptTokens (Cursor reports the uncached input only), cacheReadTokens -> CachedPromptTokens, cacheWriteTokens -> CacheCreationTokens, outputTokens -> CompletionTokens. Cursor reports no total, no reasoning count, and no cost, so TotalTokens, ReasoningTokens and CostUsd stay null.

member.name: M:PolyPrompt.Clients.CursorClient.ClassifyFailure(PolyPrompt.Clients.CliRunState,PolyPrompt.Helpers.ProcessRunResult)
member.summary: Cursor writes a run error to standard error (not as an event) and exits non-zero. When that happens after the session started, the harness reached its backend and the error is the harness's report, so it becomes the structured failure message (and is then classified as authentication, rate limit, or provider error). Without a started session the failure is classified from standard error by the base (for example a rejected argument is a crash, a missing login is not authenticated).

member.summary: Check the login with cursor-agent status --format json. The command exits with code zero whether or not a user is logged in, so the JSON isAuthenticated field decides. Account details (email, user id) are not copied into the message.

member.summary: With --stream-partial-output, deltas carry timestamp_ms and no model_call_id; the text of a segment is flushed again (with model_call_id before a tool call, without timestamp_ms at the end of the turn). The CLI also flushes the segment with a timestamp and no model_call_id before retry and interaction events, so a "delta" whose text equals the whole segment streamed so far is treated as a flush.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Clients.GeminiCliClient
member.summary:
Agent harness client for Google's Gemini CLI (gemini). This runs the CLI as a process and is unrelated to the HTTP . Each run is a headless gemini --output-format stream-json with the prompt on standard input (the CLI reads piped standard input as the prompt when no -p is given; it truncates standard input beyond 8 MB). A session is resumed with --resume <session id>; sessions are stored per project, so resume from the same working directory. Authentication is the CLI's own (Google login cached by an interactive run, or GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI/GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_GCA in the environment); the CLI has no login-status command, so connectivity cannot verify the login.
Permission mapping: and use --approval-mode default, under which a headless run denies every tool call that would need approval, so only the CLI's read-only tools run. (--approval-mode plan is deliberately not used: in headless runs the CLI switches from plan mode to YOLO mode when the plan is executed.) uses --approval-mode auto_edit (file edits are approved; shell commands still need approval and are denied). uses --approval-mode yolo. The CLI itself downgrades any mode to default in a folder the user has not trusted, and allow rules in the user's own Gemini CLI policy still apply. --sandbox is not added because it needs a container runtime or macOS Seatbelt; pass it through to opt in.

member.summary:
Map one gemini --output-format stream-json line.
init {session_id, model} -> Started (session id); model is the reported model message role=user -> (none; echo of the prompt) message role=assistant {content, delta} -> TextDelta (the text after the last tool round is the final text) tool_use {tool_name, tool_id, parameters} -> ToolUse tool_result {tool_id, status, output, error} -> ToolResult (IsError when status is "error") error {severity, message} -> Notice (IsError); the CLI uses it for non-fatal warnings and errors result status=success {stats} -> usage; Completed is emitted by the base at exit result status=error {error.message, stats} -> usage; failure (message from error, else the last error event)
Usage (from result.stats): input_tokens -> PromptTokens, cached -> CachedPromptTokens, output_tokens -> CompletionTokens, total_tokens -> TotalTokens. The CLI reports no reasoning, cache-creation, or cost figures in stream-json, so ReasoningTokens, CacheCreationTokens, and CostUsd stay null. Usage is null when stats are absent.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Clients.MuxClient
member.summary:
Agent harness client for the Mux CLI (mux). Each run is mux print --output-format jsonl with the prompt on standard input; the final text is assembled from the streamed assistant_text events (the same text --output-last-message would write), so no temporary file is used. Mux talks to whichever endpoint its own configuration (~/.mux/endpoints.json, or MUX_CONFIG_DIR) selects; picks a named endpoint and the model overrides that endpoint's model name. Mux has no login: credentials live in the endpoint configuration, and the connectivity check runs mux probe, which sends one small request to the endpoint.
This client always runs the mux CLI as a subprocess (decision D4). Hosting Mux in-process through the Mux.Core package is a possible future opt-in fast path; PolyPrompt does not reference it.
Sessions: mux print is stateless unless a session flag is given. A run resumes a session with --resume <id> (from or the provider state in the history). When is true, a new run is started under --session-id <new id> so a later run can resume it; otherwise the run reports no session id and history is replayed into the prompt.
Permission mapping (Mux's --sandbox is an application-level confinement of its own tools; it does not OS-sandbox subprocesses): uses --approval-policy auto --sandbox read-only --deny-tools web_search,web_retrieve, so only workspace reads and searches run, every mutating tool (write, edit, delete, directory changes, run_process) is refused, and the network tools are removed. uses --approval-policy auto --sandbox read-only (reads, searches, and web reads run; mutating tools are refused). uses --approval-policy auto --sandbox workspace-write --deny-tools run_process: file writes are confined to the working directory, and run_process is removed because Mux cannot confine a subprocess. uses --yolo --sandbox none. --approval-policy auto is not a bypass here: with a sandbox posture, any tool that would otherwise need an approval is refused before it runs (the equivalent of Codex's approval_policy=never inside its read-only sandbox). Subagents inherit the sandbox posture and the denied tools. A refused tool call ends the run with exit code 2, which this client reports as a failure.

member.name: M:PolyPrompt.Clients.MuxClient.ParseLine(System.String,PolyPrompt.Clients.CliRunState)
member.summary:
Map one mux print --output-format jsonl line (contract version 2).
run_started {sessionId, model} -> Started (session id when not empty; model is the reported model) assistant_text {text} -> TextDelta (the concatenation is the final text) assistant_thinking {text} -> ReasoningDelta (only with --show-thinking) tool_call_proposed {toolCall{id,name,arguments}} -> ToolUse tool_call_approved -> (none) tool_call_completed {toolCallId,toolName,result{success,content}} -> ToolResult (IsError when success is false) error, before run_started -> failure (bad flag value, unknown endpoint, missing session) error tool_call_denied|approval_error|tool_execution_error -> Notice (IsError); ToolResult (IsError) for a denied pending call; the run ends with a non-zero exit error, any other code -> failure (model request, connection, context, budget) task_plan_updated {changeKind, tasks} -> Notice (rendered task list) hook {hookEvent, hookName, outcome, message} -> Notice (IsError when blocked or warning) context_compacted -> Notice heartbeat, context_status -> (none) run_completed {status, sessionId, usage} -> usage and cost; status completed -> success, otherwise failure (max_iterations_reached is TurnLimitReached)
Usage (on run_completed): inputTokens -> PromptTokens, outputTokens -> CompletionTokens, cachedTokens -> CachedPromptTokens, reasoningTokens -> ReasoningTokens, totalTokens -> TotalTokens (Mux reports a total), and usage.costUsd -> CostUsd only when Mux reports it (the model has a rate in Mux's pricing.json). Mux's estimatedTokens is an estimate and is not mapped; CacheCreationTokens is not reported and stays null.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Clients.OpenCodeClient
member.summary:
Agent harness client for the OpenCode CLI (opencode). Each run is opencode run --format json --standalone --thinking with the prompt on standard input; a session is resumed with --session <id>. Authentication is the CLI's own (opencode auth login, provider API keys in the environment, or OpenCode's free models, which need no credentials).
Every run passes --standalone so OpenCode starts a private server as a child of the run instead of handing the turn to its shared background service: the per-run permission configuration below only reaches a server started with the run's environment (verified against OpenCode 2.2.0, whose background service ignores the client's OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT), and cancelling or timing out the run kills the whole process tree that did the work.
Permission mapping. OpenCode has no sandbox; its permissions are configuration rules (allow, ask, deny) per tool, and opencode run rejects every ask because nobody can answer it. and pin --agent build and set OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT so that, at the top level and on the build agent (agent rules take precedence over top-level rules), everything is denied ("*": "deny") except read (with .env files denied), glob, and grep. Shell commands stay denied in because OpenCode cannot limit a command to reading. adds edit (which covers OpenCode's edit, write, and patch tools) and keeps external_directory denied, so edits outside the working directory are refused; the shell stays denied because it cannot be confined to the workspace. passes --auto (approve everything not explicitly denied) and leaves OpenCode's configuration untouched. Any OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT the caller already supplies (request, client, or process environment) is kept, with its permission and agent.build.permission replaced; inline configuration that is not a JSON object is replaced, since OpenCode silently ignores invalid inline configuration.
OpenCode has no system-prompt option for run, so system instructions are prepended to the prompt. OpenCode takes its project directory from PWD rather than the process's working directory, so every run sets PWD to the run's working directory (or the current directory when none is set).

member.name: M:PolyPrompt.Clients.OpenCodeClient.ParseLine(System.String,PolyPrompt.Clients.CliRunState)
member.summary:
Map one opencode run --format json line. Every line carries the session id at the top level; the payload is in part (or error).
(first line with a sessionID) -> Started (session id) step_start -> (none; opens a step for usage accounting) text {part.text} -> TextDelta (the text of the last message is the final text) reasoning {part.text} -> ReasoningDelta (only emitted with --thinking) tool_use {part.tool, part.id, part.state} -> ToolUse, then ToolResult (OpenCode reports a tool once, when it has completed or failed; state.status "error" is IsError) step_finish {part.reason, tokens, cost} -> Notice carrying that step's usage and cost error {error.type, message, status} -> failure; Failed is emitted by the base at exit "ERROR" heading then a message (not JSON) -> failure (Crashed); the CLI's usage errors are plain text
OpenCode reports no terminal success event: a run succeeds when the process exits with code zero.
Usage: OpenCode reports tokens and cost per step (one model call); a turn is the sum of its steps, which is how OpenCode itself totals a message. Each step's values are on its Notice exactly as reported. The run's and are the sums of the step values only when every step of the turn reported a step_finish; otherwise they stay null rather than under-count (OpenCode 2.2.0 often exits before writing the final step's step_finish). tokens.input -> PromptTokens, tokens.output -> CompletionTokens, tokens.reasoning -> ReasoningTokens, tokens.cache.read -> CachedPromptTokens, tokens.cache.write -> CacheCreationTokens, tokens.total -> TotalTokens (null when not reported), cost -> CostUsd.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Clients.PiClient
member.summary:
Agent harness client for the Pi coding agent (pi), driven in RPC mode (pi --mode rpc): JSON commands on standard input, JSON responses and session events on standard output. Each run writes a get_state command (which reports the session id) and a prompt command, reads events until agent_settled, then closes standard input, which Pi treats as an orderly shutdown. A session is resumed with --session <id>. Authentication is the CLI's own (/login in Pi, ~/.pi/agent/auth.json, or provider API key environment variables such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).
Permission mapping. Pi has no sandbox and no approval prompts: an enabled tool runs with the permissions of the process, so modes are mapped to tool allowlists (--tools). and use --tools read,grep,find,ls (Pi's documented read-only set); uses --tools read,grep,find,ls,edit,write. Both leave out bash, because Pi cannot confine a shell command to the workspace or to reads. Pi does not confine edit/write to the working directory either, so WorkspaceWrite is "file edits, no shell", not a path sandbox. All three also pass --no-mcp (an allowlist alone keeps MCP tools) and --no-approve (project-local .pi settings, extensions, and other trust-gated resources are not loaded). passes none of these, so Pi's configured default tools (read, bash, edit, write unless changed), MCP servers, and project-trust decision apply.
System instructions are sent ahead of the prompt in the prompt command rather than with --append-system-prompt, because Pi reads that option's value as a file whenever it names an existing path.

member.name: M:PolyPrompt.Clients.PiClient.ParseLine(System.String,PolyPrompt.Clients.CliRunState)
member.summary:
Map one pi --mode rpc line.
response get_state {data.sessionId} -> Started (session id) response get_state success=false -> Notice (IsError) response prompt success=true "handled" -> completion (no run starts) response prompt success=true otherwise -> (none) response * success=false {error} -> failure (missing credentials are NotAuthenticated) message_update thinking_delta {delta} -> ReasoningDelta message_update text_delta {delta} -> TextDelta message_update other -> (none) message_end assistant -> usage, cost, model; its text is the final text; stopReason error|aborted is remembered as the run's error tool_execution_start -> ToolUse tool_execution_end -> ToolResult auto_retry_start {errorMessage} -> Notice (IsError) auto_retry_end success=false {finalError} -> remembered as the run's error compaction_start / compaction_end -> Notice (IsError when compaction failed) extension_error {error} -> Notice (IsError) extension_ui_request notify -> Notice extension_ui_request select|confirm|input|editor -> Notice (IsError; nobody can answer it) agent_settled aborted=true -> failure agent_settled with a remembered error -> failure agent_settled otherwise -> completion; Completed is emitted by the base at exit agent_start, agent_end, turn_*, message_start, tool_execution_update, queue_update, ... -> (none)
Usage: Pi reports usage on each assistant message, so the run's usage is the sum over its assistant messages of input -> PromptTokens, cacheRead -> CachedPromptTokens, cacheWrite -> CacheCreationTokens, output -> CompletionTokens, reasoning -> ReasoningTokens (included in output, as Pi reports it), totalTokens -> TotalTokens, and cost.total -> CostUsd. A field Pi does not report stays null.

member.summary: Check the login. When Pi has no usable model at all it reports the provider unknown, which is reported as not authenticated.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Clients.ResponsesApiClientBase
member.summary: Base class for clients that speak the Responses API (/v1/responses): , , and the xAI client. Chat, tool chat, and generation (streaming and not) go through one shared engine; provider differences (allowed values, hosted tool types, provider-only fields, and message wording) come from each client. It also hosts the native Responses operations shared by every Responses provider: , , , , , , and .
member.remarks: Requests always send store (false unless is true) and always include reasoning.encrypted_content, so a conversation continues statelessly: each response's carries the output items (including encrypted reasoning) and is replayed in order by ChatMessage.ToAssistantMessage. State from another protocol, provider, or endpoint is ignored and the plain message history is sent instead.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Clients.TypeSafeClient
member.summary:
TypeSafe client for the System One decision API (POST /v1/systemone), served by TypeSafe's hosted API (the Jev models) and by Ollaya, the local runtime for open decision models. One request asks typed questions about a state and returns calibrated answers; nothing is generated. PolyPrompt's questions are TypeSafe's noul questions. The API has no batch endpoint, so the batch overload sends requests concurrently (see ). HTTP errors, including 422 (validation), 429 (rate limit), and 529 (overloaded), are reported on the response.
Supported: Decide.
Not supported (throw ): Chat, ToolChat, Generate, Embed, SparseEmbed, Rerank, Classify, Models.
Auth: required API key, sent as a bearer token.
Defaults: decision model jev-latest.

member.summary: Initialize a TypeSafe client.
member.param: Required API key, sent as a bearer token. A local Ollaya server accepts any value.
API endpoint URL: the hosted API (default, https://api.typesafe.ai) or a local Ollaya server.
member.exception: Thrown when apiKey is null.
Thrown when apiKey is blank, contains whitespace, or looks like a URL, or endpoint is not an absolute http(s) URL.

member.name: M:PolyPrompt.Clients.TypeSafeClient.ValidateConnectivityAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Verify connectivity and credentials. Tries GET /v1/models first (served by Ollaya); when that endpoint is absent (HTTP 404, as on the hosted API), sends a minimal one-question decision instead. Returns false on an HTTP error, an unreachable server, or a timeout; rethrows only caller cancellation.
member.returns: True when the provider accepted the request.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Clients.XAiClient
member.summary:
xAI (Grok) client for the Responses API.
Supported: Chat, ToolChat, and Generate (/v1/responses, with encrypted reasoning replayed through ), the native Responses operations on , and Models (/v1/models, plus the language, embedding, image, and video catalogs).
Not supported (throw ): Embed (xAI no longer offers embedding models), SparseEmbed, Rerank, Classify, Decide.
Auth: required API key, sent as a bearer token.
Defaults: completion grok-4.7, Store = false.
xAI-only settings are on ; adds X search.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Helpers.CitationParser
member.summary: Normalizes provider citation shapes into . Spans always index the response's final Text in UTF-16 code units, end exclusive; positions inside the cited source go in . Shapes follow each provider's API reference (2026-11-12); unknown members are kept in .

member.name: M:PolyPrompt.Helpers.CitationParser.Anthropic(System.Text.Json.JsonElement)
member.summary: Anthropic Messages: text blocks carry citations[]; the span is the containing block's range in Text.

member.name: M:PolyPrompt.Helpers.CitationParser.Gemini(System.Text.Json.JsonElement)
member.summary: Gemini and Vertex AI: groundingMetadata supports joined to grounding chunks, and citationMetadata sources. Segment offsets are UTF-8 bytes of the candidate's answer text and are converted to UTF-16 indices.

member.name: M:PolyPrompt.Helpers.CitationParser.ByteToChar(System.Byte[],System.Int32)
member.summary: Convert a UTF-8 byte offset into a UTF-16 index, clamped to the text.

member.name: M:PolyPrompt.Helpers.CitationParser.Cohere(System.Text.Json.JsonElement)
member.summary: Cohere v2: message.citations[] with character offsets into the message text. Citations of thinking content are excluded (they index reasoning, not Text).

member.name: M:PolyPrompt.Helpers.CitationParser.Bedrock(System.Text.Json.JsonElement)
member.summary: Bedrock Converse: citationsContent blocks; each citation has a location union (document char, page, or chunk, search result, or web). Spans in the response text are not reported, so TextStart/TextEnd are null.

member.name: M:PolyPrompt.Helpers.CitationParser.ChatCompletions(System.Text.Json.JsonElement)
member.summary: Chat Completions: choices[0].message.annotations[] with nested url_citation. Offsets are kept as reported (whether end_index is inclusive is not documented).

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Helpers.PolyPromptJsonContext
member.summary: Source-generated JSON metadata for PolyPrompt's wire shapes and public models. It lets PolyPrompt run without reflection under Native AOT and trimming, and lets applications persist conversations and responses the same way, for example JsonSerializer.Serialize(messages, PolyPromptJsonContext.Default.ListChatMessage). Settings match : null properties omitted, enums as strings, dates as UTC ISO 8601, and tolerant reads. Decision questions and answers are abstract, polymorphic types and are not included.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Helpers.Serializer
member.summary: JSON serializer used by PolyPrompt clients, built on System.Text.Json and safe for Native AOT and trimming. Untyped values (object, Dictionary<string, object>, List<object>) deserialize to . Null properties are omitted when writing (dictionary entries are always written), enums are written as strings, and reads tolerate trailing commas, comments, and numbers written as strings.
member.remarks: Graphs made of dictionaries, lists, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, enums, dates, GUIDs, byte arrays, , , and are written without reflection. Any other type is resolved through, in order: resolvers registered with , , and reflection when the application allows it (). In a Native AOT or trimmed application reflection is off, so a type outside those sources raises ; register a source-generated that includes it, or use an overload that takes a .

Registered resolvers are consulted before and apply to every PolyPrompt client in the process. Registering the same resolver twice has no effect.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Models.CliPermissionMode
member.summary: What an agent harness may do to the machine it runs on. Each harness client maps these modes to the closest flags its CLI offers; the mapping is documented on each client. The default everywhere is , and no client ever defaults to a mode that bypasses approvals or sandboxing.

member.name: F:PolyPrompt.Models.CliPermissionMode.Restricted
member.summary: The most conservative mode the harness offers: read-only tools only, and anything that would need an approval is denied because nobody is there to approve it. This is the default.

member.name: F:PolyPrompt.Models.CliPermissionMode.ReadOnly
member.summary: The harness may read the workspace and run read-only commands, but may not modify files.

member.name: F:PolyPrompt.Models.CliPermissionMode.WorkspaceWrite
member.summary: The harness may edit files inside the working directory without asking. Commands outside the workspace or with network access stay restricted where the harness can enforce it.

member.name: F:PolyPrompt.Models.CliPermissionMode.Unrestricted
member.summary: Approvals and sandboxing are bypassed. Only use this inside an environment that is already isolated.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Models.CompletionOptions
member.summary: Settings for completion operations (chat, tool chat, and text generation), shared by every provider. The same type serves two roles: a completion client's Defaults, and the per-call options passed to an operation. For each setting, a non-null per-call value wins, otherwise the client default is used, otherwise the provider's own default applies (no field is sent). Provider-specific settings live on derived types such as OllamaCompletionOptions, which merge the same way.

member.name: P:PolyPrompt.Models.CompletionOptions.Model
member.summary: Model name. On a client's Defaults this is the client's model (the client's Model property reads and writes it); per call it overrides that model. Default: null.

member.name: P:PolyPrompt.Models.CompletionOptions.MaxTokens
member.summary: Maximum number of tokens to generate. Clamped to 1..10,000,000. When no value is set anywhere, 4096 is sent. Default: null.

member.name: P:PolyPrompt.Models.CompletionOptions.Temperature
member.summary: Sampling temperature. Clamped to 0.0..2.0. Null sends no value, so the provider default applies. Default: null.

member.name: P:PolyPrompt.Models.CompletionOptions.TopP
member.summary: Nucleus sampling (top-p). Clamped to 0.0..1.0. Null sends no value, so the provider default applies. Default: null.

member.name: P:PolyPrompt.Models.CompletionOptions.SystemPrompt
member.summary: System prompt. Sent with chat calls, and with tool chat calls whose messages contain no system message. Text generation sends its prompt unchanged and ignores this setting. Default: null.

member.name: P:PolyPrompt.Models.CompletionOptions.ReasoningEffort
member.summary: Reasoning ("thinking") effort for reasoning-capable models, applied to chat and tool chat. Null sends no reasoning field, so the provider's own default applies. turns thinking off where the provider allows it (Ollama think: false, a Gemini thinking budget of 0, Cohere and Bedrock thinking disabled); other levels map to each provider's effort or budget as described on . Text generation ignores this setting. Default: null.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Models.RerankOptions
member.summary: Settings for rerank operations, shared by every provider. The same type serves as a rerank client's Defaults and as per-call options; a non-null per-call value wins over the client default.

member.name: P:PolyPrompt.Models.RerankOptions.Model
member.summary: Model name. On a client's Defaults this is the client's model; per call it overrides that model. Ignored by Text Embeddings Inference, which serves a single model. Default: null.

member.name: P:PolyPrompt.Models.RerankOptions.TopN
member.summary: Maximum number of results to return, highest score first. Null returns a score for every document. Minimum 1. A per-call value cannot exceed the number of documents passed to RerankAsync, which is checked when the request is made; a value from the client's Defaults is instead capped at the number of documents. Providers without a native top-N parameter (Text Embeddings Inference) score every document and the list is trimmed client-side. Default: null.
member.exception: Thrown when set to a value less than 1.

member.name: P:PolyPrompt.Models.RerankOptions.ReturnDocuments
member.summary: When true, each is populated with the text of the document it scores. The text is taken from the caller's input list by index, so no extra data is requested from the provider. Null means false unless the client's Defaults sets it. Default: null.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Models.RerankResponse
member.summary: Response from a rerank request. Results are always sorted by score, highest first, regardless of the order the provider returned them in, and each result's Index refers back to the caller's input list.

member.summary: Provider-assigned response identifier, when the provider returns one (Cohere). Null otherwise.

member.summary: Scored documents, highest score first. Empty when the request failed.

member.name: P:PolyPrompt.Models.RerankResponse.SearchUnits
member.summary: Billed search units, when the provider reports them (Cohere). Null otherwise.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Models.RerankResult
member.summary: A single scored document from a rerank request.

member.name: P:PolyPrompt.Models.RerankResult.Index
member.summary: Zero-based position of the scored document in the list passed to RerankAsync.

member.name: P:PolyPrompt.Models.RerankResult.Score
member.summary: Relevance score for the document. Higher is more relevant. Scores are provider-specific and are not comparable across providers: Cohere, VoyageAI, and Bedrock return a normalized 0..1 relevance, while Text Embeddings Inference returns a sigmoid-normalized 0..1 score by default or raw logits (any real number) when raw scores are requested.

member.name: P:PolyPrompt.Models.RerankResult.Document
member.summary: Text of the scored document. Populated only when is true; otherwise null.

member.name: T:PolyPrompt.Wire.EventStreamDecoder
member.summary: Decoder for the AWS application/vnd.amazon.eventstream binary framing used by Bedrock's ConverseStream / InvokeModelWithResponseStream responses. Unlike the SSE/NDJSON streams every other provider uses, this is a length-prefixed binary protocol: each message is a 12-byte prelude (total length, headers length, prelude CRC-32), a headers block, a payload, and a trailing message CRC-32. Both CRCs are validated to detect stream desynchronization.

member.name: M:PolyPrompt.Wire.EventStreamDecoder.DecodeAsync(System.IO.Stream,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Asynchronously decode a stream of AWS event-stream messages until the underlying stream ends.
member.returns: An async sequence of decoded messages.
member.exception: Thrown when a CRC check fails or a frame is truncated.

member.summary: Encode a single event-stream message: prelude (with CRC), string-valued headers, payload, and the trailing message CRC. Provided so tests (and any producer) can generate byte-accurate frames the decoder round-trips.
